en: to pick out; to sort out

examples.ko: 밭에서 돌멩이를 골라내는 일이 의외로 힘들어요.
examples.en: Picking stones out of the field is surprisingly hard.

examples.ko: 분리배출이 잘 안 되면 재활용 공장에서 다시 골라내야 해서 비용이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: If recycling isn't sorted well, the factory has to pick things out again, which costs a lot.

examples.ko: 밥에서 콩을 골라내지 말고 다 먹어요.
examples.en: Don't pick the beans out of your rice, eat them all.

examples.ko: 상한 과일만 골라내고 나머지는 씻어 두세요.
examples.en: Pick out only the spoiled fruit and wash the rest.

examples.ko: 사진이 많아서 잘 나온 것만 골라냈어요.
examples.en: There were many photos, so I picked out only the good ones.
People check each item one by one to pick out the defective ones.

explain: '고르다'는 원하는 것을 선택하는 말이고, '골라내다'는 섞여 있는 것 중에서 필요 없거나 문제 있는 것을 따로 빼내는 데 많이 써요. '잘 나온 사진만 골라내다'처럼 좋은 것만 뽑을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I picked out the rotten fruit and threw it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 것을 가려내서 치울 때 자주 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pattern for sorting out bad items and getting rid of them.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick out and throw away

phrases.example: 콩 속의 작은 돌을 가려내야 해요.
phrases.en: You have to sort out the small stones from the beans.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골라내다'와 비슷하게 섞인 것에서 구별해 뺄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '골라내다', it means separating something out from a mixture.

phrases.example: 사진 중에서 잘 나온 것만 골라냈어요.
phrases.en: I picked out only the photos that turned out well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요 없는 것이 아니라 좋은 것만 뽑을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also mean picking only the good ones, not just removing the bad.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick out only the good ones

explain_en: Sort out — pick certain items from a group, often to remove them. '고르다' means choosing what you want, while '골라내다' is mostly used for pulling unwanted or faulty things out of a mixed group. It is also used for picking out only the good ones, as in '잘 나온 사진만 골라내다'.

examples.en: The company ended up taking on all the losses.
My older brother took over our parents' debt.

examples.ko: 문제가 생기면 결국 제가 책임을 떠안아요.
examples.en: When a problem comes up, I end up shouldering the responsibility.

examples.ko: 남이 한 실수까지 떠안을 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't need to take on even the mistakes other people made.

examples.ko: 그는 가족의 생계를 떠안고 일찍 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: He took on supporting his family and started working early.

examples.ko: 아무도 그 위험을 떠안으려 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: No one wanted to take on that risk.

explain: 빚, 책임, 손실, 부담처럼 무거운 것을 다른 사람 대신 또는 어쩔 수 없이 맡아서 지는 것이에요. 비슷한 '떠맡다'와 가깝고, 남에게 넘기는 쪽은 '떠맡기다'예요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고 부담이 되는 것에 써요.

phrases.en: The team leader took on the responsibility for the failure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 책임을 대신 지는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes on a heavy responsibility on behalf of others.

phrases.en: I suddenly ended up taking on a big burden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어쩔 수 없이 맡게 되었다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling of having no choice but to take it on.

phrases.example: 투자하면 손해 볼 위험을 떠안아야 해요.
phrases.en: If you invest, you have to bear the risk of loss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험이나 손해처럼 부담이 되는 것을 감수할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for accepting burdens such as risk or loss.

explain_en: Take a burden or responsibility onto yourself. It means taking on something heavy, such as debt, responsibility, loss or a burden, in someone's place or because you have no choice. It is close to '떠맡다', and the side that hands it off uses '떠맡기다'. It is not used for good things, only for things that weigh on you.

examples.en: You have to clean up your dog's waste on the street.
Animal waste smells strong.
I had a stool and urine test at the hospital.
My car got dirty because of bird droppings.

examples.ko: 화장실 청소는 배설물이 쌓이지 않게 자주 해야 해요.
examples.en: You should clean the bathroom often so waste doesn't pile up.

examples.ko: 배설물로 몸 상태를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell your health condition from your waste.

explain: 배설물은 대변과 소변을 함께 가리키는 말이라 의학, 동물, 위생 이야기에서 써요. 일상에서는 '똥', '오줌'이라고도 하지만 점잖게 말할 때는 배설물이 나아요.

phrases.en: Watch out for animal waste in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물의 대변과 소변을 점잖게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to refer to animal feces and urine.

phrases.en: I clean up the dog's waste during walks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗하게 하는 일을 말할 때 '치우다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 치우다 for cleaning up.

phrases.en: There's a smell of waste in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새가 나는 원인을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the source of a smell.

explain_en: 배설물 covers both stool and urine, so it is used in medical, animal, and hygiene contexts. In daily talk people also say 똥 and 오줌, but 배설물 sounds more polite.

examples.en: The kids are chatting in whispers.

examples.ko: 엄마가 소곤소곤 말해서 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: Mom spoke so softly that I couldn't hear well.
I whispered with the person next to me in the theater.
The baby is sleeping, so please speak softly.
I listened closely to the whispering sound.

examples.ko: 둘이 소곤소곤 비밀 얘기를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering secrets.

explain: 작은 소리로 조용히 말하는 모양을 나타내서 '말하다', '이야기하다'와 자주 함께 써요. 시끄러운 '떠들썩'이나 '왁자지껄'과 반대되는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: You have to speak in whispers in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용한 곳에서 작게 말하라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to tell someone to talk quietly in a quiet place.

phrases.example: 그가 내 귀에 대고 소곤소곤 속삭였어요.
phrases.en: He whispered softly into my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이에서 비밀처럼 말하는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a feeling of speaking secretly up close.

phrases.en: I can hear whispered talking from the next room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들리는 소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a sound that you hear.

explain_en: Soft, gentle whispering, often cute and friendly (소곤소곤) It shows a quiet, low-voiced way of talking and often goes with '말하다' or '이야기하다'. It is the opposite in feel of noisy words like '떠들썩' or '왁자지껄'.

t90.ax: The kids are chatting in whispers.

en: to mimic; to go through the motions

examples.ko: 동생은 자는 시늉하면서 제 말을 다 들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling pretended to sleep while listening to everything I said.

examples.ko: 아이가 의사처럼 청진기를 대는 시늉을 해요.
examples.en: The child pretends to put a stethoscope on like a doctor.

examples.ko: 그는 바쁜 시늉을 했지만 사실 할 일이 없었어요.
examples.en: He pretended to be busy, but he actually had nothing to do.

examples.ko: 친구가 우는 시늉을 하며 저를 웃겼어요.
examples.en: My friend made me laugh by pretending to cry.

examples.ko: 모르는 시늉하지 말고 솔직하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't pretend you don't know, and tell me honestly.
Don't just go through the motions of studying, focus.

explain: '~는 시늉을 하다'로 띄어 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 흔해요. 진짜는 아닌데 그런 모습이나 동작을 겉으로 흉내 낸다는 느낌이라서, '척하다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The child is pretending to sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form.

phrases.en: My younger sibling joked by pretending to cry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜가 아닌 흉내를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a fake imitation.

phrases.en: He pretended not to know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning and more casual.

explain_en: It is much more common to say '~는 시늉을 하다' as separate words. It means imitating the look or motion of something without it being real, so it can often be used much like '척하다'.

dis.h: Pretend by making a gesture or motion
gh: Pose as someone or something else; disguise

p.n: 가장하다 does not fit an acted motion like crying; it means posing as a person or thing.

en: to explore; to probe in order to find something

examples.en: A robot explores the inside of the cave.

examples.ko: 학생들이 자기에게 맞는 진로를 탐색하고 있어요.
examples.en: The students are exploring career paths that suit them.

examples.ko: 새로운 시장을 탐색한 뒤에 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: We made a plan after exploring the new market.
The police searched the area around the scene.
I learned how to search for information on the internet.
I'll look into several options and then decide.

explain: 필요한 것을 찾으려고 조심스럽게 살펴볼 때 써요. '찾다'보다 격식 있고, 범위를 넓게 훑는 느낌이 있어요. 진로, 시장, 방법 앞에 자주 오고 '탐색 중이에요'라는 말도 많이 해요.

phrases.en: I'll explore several methods first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'가 붙어 시험 삼아 살펴본다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' gives a sense of trying out and looking over.

phrases.example: 저는 지금 새 일자리를 탐색 중이에요.
phrases.en: I'm currently exploring new job options.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 결정하지 않고 찾아보는 중일 때 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when still searching and not yet decided.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the middle of exploring

phrases.en: The team members explore ways to solve the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 해결할 길을 찾아본다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to look for a way to solve a problem.

explain_en: Carefully search a place or data to find something (단서를 탐색하다) Used when carefully looking around to find something you need. It is more formal than '찾다' and suggests scanning a wide area. It often goes with career paths, markets, and methods, and '탐색 중이에요' (I'm exploring) is a common phrase.

t90.ax: A robot explores the inside of the cave.

examples.en: My throat stung, so I drank a lot of water.
The arm where I got the shot still stings.
Shampoo got in my eyes and they stung.

examples.ko: 약을 바르면 조금 따끔거릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: It may sting a little when you apply the medicine.
My sunburned skin stings, what should I do?
The mosquito bite stung and then started to itch.

explain: '따끔하다'는 한 번 찌르는 듯 짧게 아플 때 많이 쓰고, '따끔거리다'는 그 느낌이 계속 되풀이될 때 써요. 목, 눈, 상처, 피부처럼 쓰라린 곳에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: It stings for a moment when you get a shot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 한 번 찌르듯 아플 때 써요. '따끔거리다'는 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a brief, single prick; 따끔거리다 is for when it keeps recurring.

phrases.en: My eyes sting, maybe because dust got in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 쓰라리고 아플 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for eyes that feel sore and irritated.

phrases.en: My throat feels prickly, maybe because I caught a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따끔따끔'을 쓰면 여러 번 찌르는 듯한 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated 따끔따끔 makes the repeated prickling feeling clearer.

explain_en: '따끔하다' is often used for a brief prick, while '따끔거리다' is used when that stinging feeling keeps repeating. It fits sore spots like the throat, eyes, wounds and skin.

t90.ax: Shampoo got in my eyes and they stung.

examples.ko: 아기를 낳고 한 달 동안 몸조리를 했어요.
examples.en: After giving birth, I rested and recovered for a month.

examples.ko: 감기 심하게 걸렸다면서요? 푹 쉬고 몸조리 잘하세요.
examples.en: I heard you caught a bad cold. Rest well and take care of yourself.
After surgery, you have to rest and recover at home.
My mom came to help me with my recovery.
If you don't take care of yourself during recovery, you'll suffer later.
After leaving the hospital, I recovered at my country house.

explain: 아프거나 아기를 낳은 뒤에 쉬면서 건강을 되찾는 것이에요. 아픈 사람에게 '몸조리 잘하세요'라고 하면 '푹 쉬고 잘 회복하세요'라는 인사말이 돼요. 출산 후에는 '산후조리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I rested at home to recover after the surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 쉬면서 몸을 회복하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 하다, it describes the act of resting to regain health.

phrases.en: My mom came to help me recover after giving birth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 낳은 뒤의 몸조리만 말해서 더 좁은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A narrower term that refers only to recovery after childbirth.

phrases.en: Get well soon. Take good care of yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 쓰는 반말 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An informal way to say it to a close friend.

explain_en: It means resting and regaining your health after an illness or childbirth. Telling a sick person '몸조리 잘하세요' works as a greeting meaning 'rest well and recover'. After childbirth it is also called '산후조리'.

examples.en: This sweater can only be hand-washed.
Lukewarm water is best for hand-washing.
The clothing label says hand wash.
If you hand-wash, clothes get less damaged.
The washing machine has a hand-wash cycle.
After hand-washing, dry it in the shade.

explain: 세탁기를 쓰는 '기계 세탁'과 반대되는 말이에요. 옷 라벨이나 세탁 설명에서 많이 보고, 대화에서는 '손빨래'라고도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: This coat can be hand-washed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 설명에서 손으로 빨 수 있다는 표시로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in clothing descriptions to say hand-washing is okay.

phrases.en: There is a hand-wash symbol on the clothing label.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁 방법을 알려 주는 그림이나 글을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the symbol or text showing how to wash.

phrases.en: Hand-washing is hard, so I use a washing machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual word used in conversation.

explain_en: Sino-Korean; care labels, recommendations, laundry services. It is the opposite of machine washing. You see it on clothing labels and in laundry instructions, and in conversation people often say '손빨래' too.

t90.ax: The clothing label says hand wash.

examples.en: I went to the hospital to get a flu shot.
The flu spread widely this winter.

examples.ko: 아이가 인플루엔자에 걸려서 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: My child caught the flu and couldn't go to school.
My fever was so high that I thought it was the flu.
I rested for a week because of the flu.
The flu test result will come out tomorrow.

explain: 일상에서는 '독감'이라는 말을 훨씬 많이 쓰고, 인플루엔자는 병원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 그냥 '감기'와 달리 열이 높고 몸이 많이 아파요. '독감에 걸리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I caught the flu and rested for a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 인플루엔자 대신 '독감'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 독감 is used much more than 인플루엔자.

phrases.en: My company gives flu shots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 공공 안내에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the formal phrase used at hospitals and in public notices.

phrases.en: There are many flu patients at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린 사람을 말할 때 뒤에 '환자'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 환자 to refer to people who have the illness.

explain_en: In daily life people say 독감 much more often; 인플루엔자 is used at hospitals and in the news. Unlike a plain 감기 (cold), it brings a high fever and body aches. You say 독감에 걸리다 for catching it.

examples.en: The spring rain softly moistened the earth all night.

examples.ko: 피부를 촉촉이 유지하려고 물을 많이 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink a lot of water to keep my skin moist.
Morning dew formed softly on the blades of grass.

examples.ko: 빗속을 걷다 보니 머리가 촉촉이 젖었어요.
examples.en: After walking in the rain, my hair got damp.
My eyes grew moist while watching the movie.

examples.ko: 마른 화분에 물을 주어 흙을 촉촉이 적셨어요.
examples.en: I watered the dry flowerpot and moistened the soil.

explain: 조금 젖어서 부드럽고 눈에 띄게 습기가 있는 모양을 말해요. '적시다, 젖다, 맺히다' 같은 동사와 같이 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '촉촉하게'도 같은 뜻으로 자연스럽게 써요.

phrases.example: 비 온 뒤라 땅이 촉촉하게 젖었어요.
phrases.en: Since it rained, the ground got moist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '촉촉이'보다 더 자주 쓰는 자연스러운 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used more often than '촉촉이' in speech.

phrases.en: If you put on cream, your skin feels moist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '촉촉하다'의 해요체로, 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of the adjective, describing a state.

phrases.en: I like moist bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 부드럽고 수분이 있을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for soft, moist food.

explain_en: It describes something lightly wet, soft and visibly damp. It often appears with verbs like '적시다', '젖다' and '맺히다'. In speech, '촉촉하게' is also a natural way to say the same thing.

t90.ax: After walking in the rain, my hair got damp.

examples.en: We ordered flatfish sashimi at a raw fish restaurant.
Flatfish has chewy, clean-tasting flesh.
Today I bought a fresh flatfish at the market.
I like sushi made with flatfish the best.
I like salmon more than flatfish.

examples.ko: 수족관 바닥에 광어가 납작하게 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: A flatfish was lying flat on the bottom of the tank.

explain: 생선 이름으로는 '넙치'도 있지만, 횟집이나 식당에서는 '광어'라고 말해요. 보통 '광어회'처럼 회로 먹는 생선으로 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: I bought one flatfish at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fish are counted with '마리'.

phrases.example: 저는 초밥 중에서 광어 초밥을 제일 좋아해요.
phrases.en: Among sushi, I like flatfish sushi the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당 메뉴에서 자주 보는 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A food name you often see on restaurant menus.

phrases.en: Neopchi is another name for gwangeo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 생선을 부르는 다른 이름이고, 식당에서는 '광어'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same fish; restaurants more often say '광어'.

explain_en: The fish also has the name '넙치', but at raw fish restaurants and in daily talk people say '광어'. You most often meet it as a sashimi fish, as in '광어회'.

examples.en: I mixed a raw egg into my rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 날달걀을 먹으면 배탈이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Eating raw eggs can give you a stomachache.
Beat one raw egg into the bowl.
There are three raw eggs in the fridge.

examples.ko: 날달걀과 삶은 달걀은 돌려 보면 구별돼요.
examples.en: You can tell a raw egg from a boiled one by spinning it.
Please crack raw eggs carefully so the shell doesn't fall in.

explain: 익히지 않은 달걀은 '날달걀'이나 '생달걀'이라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '날달걀'이 더 자주 들려요. 반대말은 '삶은 달걀', '구운 달걀'처럼 조리 방법으로 말해요. '날계란'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I keep raw eggs in the fridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 포장이나 요리 설명에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; often seen on packaging and in cooking instructions.

phrases.en: I put a raw egg into the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '날달걀'과 같은 뜻으로 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in speech with the same meaning as 날달걀.

phrases.en: I crack a raw egg into a bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 '깨다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 깨다 when cooking.

explain_en: An uncooked egg is called '날달걀' or '생달걀', and '날달걀' is heard more in daily talk. The opposites are described by cooking method, like '삶은 달걀' (boiled egg) and '구운 달걀' (baked egg). People also say '날계란'.

examples.en: I made broth with anchovies and kelp.
Kelp gets soft when you soak it in water.
I eat fried kelp chips as a snack.
I bought dried kelp at the market.
The broth is clean-tasting because kelp went into it.

examples.ko: 삶은 다시마에 밥과 고기를 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped rice and meat in boiled kelp and ate it.

explain: 미역과 비슷하지만 다시마는 더 두껍고 넓어서 주로 국물을 낼 때 써요. 멸치와 함께 넣어 육수를 내는 게 가장 흔해요.

phrases.en: I made noodles with kelp broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시마를 우려낸 국물을 말하고, 요리할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broth made by steeping kelp, common in cooking.

phrases.en: I soak the kelp before making soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마른 다시마를 물에 담가 부드럽게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for soaking dried kelp to make it soft.

phrases.en: I made stew with anchovy and kelp stock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 요리에서 가장 흔한 육수 조합이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common stock combination in Korean cooking.

explain_en: It looks like 미역 but 다시마 is thicker and wider, and it is mainly used to make broth. Boiling it together with anchovies for 육수 is the most common use.
